answer: Harbour dues payment history with berth allocation record is the check: berths paid for at one harbour season after season. A farm faking 328 aliases needs 328 separate berth records, each built over years, so the cost multiplies per alias instead of staying flat. The nectar test is the price tag: 328 fakes mean 328 payments. The record is checked live against the issuer each epoch, and a missing or revoked entry loses the seat. The kernel signal is visible to every grader, and the lagoon ledger is what makes the farm's arithmetic fail.
